stories.why_it_matters: The meeting sets IORA's next policy steps on Indian Ocean trade, shipping and security at a time of war-hit sea routes in the Gulf and Red Sea.

image.alt: A row of national flags of Indian Ocean Rim Association member countries

stories.headline: India hosts 25th IORA foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi today
stories.summary: Ministers and senior officials from 23 Indian Ocean Rim Association members and 12 dialogue partners meet in New Delhi under India's 2025-27 chairship. On the eve of the meeting, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate talks with the foreign ministers of Sri Lanka, Maldives, Seychelles and Mauritius.

stories.headline: Sitharaman ends pre-budget talks for 2027-28 with a first-ever youth session
stories.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held the 13th and last pre-budget consultation for the 2027-28 Union Budget, with young people, in New Delhi on Thursday evening. The talks began on 16 November and drew more than 200 participants from 13 groups; the youth suggestions covered jobs, manufacturing, farming, housing and education.

stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on Saudi refineries add a war-risk premium to crude, which raises India's import bill and weighs on the rupee.
stories.note: Strike and damage reported by Saudi Energy Ministry; blame on the Houthis is a claim by the Saudi-led coalition, not independently confirmed.

image.alt: File photo: smoke rises behind trucks on a road after an attack on a Saudi oil facility in October

impact.why: A strike on a large Saudi refinery raises fears for Gulf oil supply.
Dearer crude lifts India's import bill and dollar demand.

stories.headline: Strike on Saudi Jazan refinery kills a worker; coalition says Houthis did it
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry says a projectile hit the 400,000-barrel-a-day Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker, injuring several others and halting some operations. The Saudi-led coalition says the Houthis carried out the attack and that it destroyed the missile launcher in Yemen's Hodeidah. The Houthis have not commented.

stories.why_it_matters: The new ECB chief will steer euro interest rates, which move the euro and global bond markets.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera (reporting Antonio Costa's announcement).

impact.why: A new ECB chief may change the bank's rate path from next year.

stories.headline: Euro zone picks Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
stories.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa said euro zone leaders agreed to recommend Pablo Hernandez de Cos, head of the Bank for International Settlements and a former Bank of Spain governor, as the next ECB president. He would take over in February, when Christine Lagarde leaves early; formal appointment is expected at the December EU summit.

stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera. Both sides' statements are their own claims.

impact.why: Talk of a deal could ease the war premium, but attacks on Gulf states continue.

stories.headline: Update: Iran denies Kuwait drone attack and calls it 'suspicious'
stories.summary: New since last night: Iran denied carrying out the drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italians. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the incident suspicious and a "pre-cooked recipe for war". US President Donald Trump says Washington has "victory at hand" and is giving Tehran a chance to negotiate a deal.

stories.headline: EU leaders fail to agree long-term budget and new $49bn Ukraine loan
stories.summary: EU leaders in Brussels stayed split on Thursday over a roughly $1.76 trillion budget for 2028-34 and a $49 billion loan for Ukraine next year, with talks possibly running into Friday. Italy's Giorgia Meloni said the sides were "light-years away", and Germany's Friedrich Merz threatened to hold up the budget without a joint commitment to Ukraine.

stories.why_it_matters: A firm dollar and expected Fed hike keep pressure on the rupee, which closed at 92.44 on Thursday.

impact.why: A firm dollar and Fed hike bets weigh on emerging-market currencies.
Markets almost fully expect a December Fed rate rise.

stories.headline: Dollar holds near 2026 highs in holiday trade as Fed hike bets stay near 96%
stories.summary: The dollar index stayed near 103.7 in thin Thanksgiving trading, just below this year's peak. The euro slipped about 0.2% to $1.096 and the yen held near 159.2 per dollar, close to the 160 level that brought Japanese intervention earlier this year. CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December Fed rate rise at about 96%.

stories.note: Single source: Trading Economics (Japan statistics data).

impact.why: Faster inflation supports a BoJ hike, but the miss versus forecast tempers it.

stories.headline: Tokyo core inflation rises to 2.9% in November, just under forecasts
stories.summary: Core consumer prices in Tokyo's central wards rose 2.9% from a year earlier in November, up from 2.6% in October but slightly below the 3.0% economists expected. The data came out early Friday, India time.

stories.why_it_matters: Crude near $96 raises India's import bill and costs for oil marketers, airlines and paint makers.
stories.note: Prices differ by time of quote: Bloomberg 'near $96', All India Radio $95.38 at about 8 PM IST.

impact.why: Gulf refinery attacks and the OPEC+ meeting keep supply risks in focus.
Higher crude squeezes margins of fuel retailers.
Costlier oil raises India's dollar demand.

stories.headline: Brent trades near $96 after Saudi refinery strike; OPEC+ meets on Sunday
stories.summary: Brent crude traded near $96 a barrel on Thursday after rising almost 6% over two sessions, as the strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery added to Gulf supply worries; All India Radio put Brent at $95.38, up 0.8%, and WTI at $84.65 in the evening. US trading was thin for Thanksgiving. OPEC+ meets on Sunday, when it may roll current output quotas into January.

impact.why: Futures point to gains in a thin holiday session.
Firm global cues support Indian shares at the open.

stories.headline: US stock futures rise 0.7% before a half-day session; Asia opens higher
stories.summary: S&P 500 futures rose 0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures 0.6% on Thursday evening ahead of Friday's shortened session, which ends at 1 p.m. New York time. The S&P 500 is up 3.9% this week so far and the Nasdaq 4.3%. In early Asian trade on Friday, Japan's Nikkei rose 0.3%, Korea's Kospi 0.6% and Australia's ASX 200 0.4%.

stories.note: Spot gold. COMEX December futures in the snapshot trade at a higher price.

impact.why: Expected Fed rate rises reduce the appeal of non-yielding gold.

stories.headline: Gold slips back toward $3,550-3,565 as Fed hike bets weigh
stories.summary: Spot gold eased in Asian trade on Friday to the mid-$3,500s after briefly topping $3,600 on Thursday, as traders priced an almost certain US rate rise in December. It is still well above Wednesday's 15-month low near $3,427.

forex_results.title: Tokyo Core CPI y/y
forex_results.why: Tokyo inflation rose but came in just below the 3.0% forecast, slightly easing pressure on the Bank of Japan to hike.
